summary: This is a simple test case that verifies the boolean value true evaluates as true. It shows two equivalent ways to make this assertion in PHP testing—one using an older method and one using a newer, more modern syntax. The comment indicates that only one of these assertion lines should be kept since they accomplish the same thing.

explanations.3: test() is a function that defines a single test case with a name and a callback function containing the actual test logic.
explanations.5: $this->assertTrue(true) is the traditional way to assert that a value is true; it's a method call on the test object.
explanations.6: expect(true)->toBeTrue() is a newer, more readable syntax for the same assertion; it uses a fluent interface where you wrap a value in expect() and chain a matcher like toBeTrue().
